key_insight: V-PaSS improves prediction for unfamiliar perovskite solar cells by representing alloy physics and device interfaces rather than treating materials as arbitrary labels.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help screen new absorber compositions and device stacks before fabrication, including combinations absent from training data.
method: Interpolate relaxed crystal graphs of 23 pure ABX₃ endpoints using Vegard’s law with learned bandgap bowing.
Encode layer sequence, n-i-p or p-i-n polarity, and interfacial band offsets.
Represent chemical descriptions with a scientific language model.
evidence_signal: Under institution-grouped evaluation with unseen test laboratories, untuned V-PaSS achieved 2.861% MAE versus 3.017% for a gradient-boosted baseline, with reported error reductions of 15.7–19.0% on unseen absorber alloys.
watch_item: Extrapolation depends on the endpoint library and alloy-interpolation assumptions; the abstract does not establish reliability for compositions outside that physical representation.
paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
